newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria foreign reserves reach $6.4 bln on Aug 4.
newsitem.headline: Algeria foreign reserves reach $6.4 bln on Aug 4.

text.p: Algeria's foreign reserves reached $6.4 billion on Monday, the highest since 1981, the official Algerian news agency APS quoted official finance sources as saying.
"The foreign reserves at the moment have reached $6.4 billion, the equivalent of seven months of imports," APS said.
Algeria's foreign reserves rose by more than $1.0 billion since last March when they were at $5.3 billion, according to official figures.
They stood at $4.2 billion in December 1996 compared to $2.11 billion in the same period in 1995, official data showed.
The Algerian government said last week that Algerian crude oil had earned more than a conservative budgeted traget of $17.50 a barrel in the past seven months. It gave no details.
The North African country's average crude price stood at $21.6 per barrel in 1996 compared to a budgeted average of $16-$17 per barrel in the same year.
The value of Algeria's exports of oil and gas, amounting to more than 90 percent of its total export, rose to $12.6 billion in 1996, up 29 percent from 1995.
